name: Jizrahiah
title: Levitical Head in the Time of David
summary: Jizrahiah (also spelled Izrihijah) was a Levite from the clan of Kohath who served under King David. He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as one of the heads among the Levites who had administrative and spiritual duties in Israel. His role was connected to the organization of temple service and Levitical administration.

keyEvents.title: Listed among the descendants of Kohath
keyEvents.description: Jizrahiah is mentioned as one of the sons of Kohath among the Levitical clans that were organized under King David's rule.

keyEvents.title: Levitical Service under David
keyEvents.description: Izrahiah was among the Levites who received specific tasks in connection with organizing worship and administration in Israel during David's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Kohathite Clan
keyEvents.description: As part of the Kohathite clan, Izrahiah belonged to one of the most prominent Levitical families responsible for service at the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: Registration of the Levitical Families
keyEvents.description: In the great registration of the Levitical families carried out by David, Izrahiah and his family were carefully recorded to ensure proper assignment of duties.
